P3: I don’t know exactly how much of the future fear is accurate. AI may make human life enormously better, suck millions of people out of their jobs, wind up as a sort of admin layer between us and nearly everything - or do all three before Chantress Seba gets through her commune applications. 😂
P4: For me, investing in more human independence beats waiting for certainty. I'd take having community and finding out I didn't need an exit over needing one after spending ten years optimizing my feed. 😂
P5: What connections to the technosphere would be useful to limit or keep if you were to design a community?
P6: Medical care, banking, phones, vehicles, schools, supply chains, government ID, internet and energy are each a separate decision. If you opt out of them completely, it can cause needless suffering. If you depend on them completely, the outside system can reach directly into every essential function.
P7: The Amish, over generations, have made community decisions about where and if they want to use a piece of technology based on how it affects their community. Different Amish communities make different decisions. Some use it at work but restrict it at home. Some share it instead of everyone owning one. Others hold off on using it until they know more about its social effects. Whatever else you think of the Amish, they at least understand that adopting a technology is a decision for the group to make, and that it shouldn't get downloaded onto your device while you sleep.
P8: Medical care is one of the toughest connections to work out. A community may prefer natural care, but what happens if someone in the community needs trauma surgery, antibiotics, dentistry, emergency obstetric care, or any number of specialist services? The community really needs to hash out in advance how people in it are going to have access to these services. What will be guaranteed out of what the community shares? What may require money from outside sources (or insurance)? And how will it treat people who want different levels of care?
P9: No member should have to jump through ideological hoops when they're scared or sick. If someone in the community gets catastrophically ill, there should already be an agreement in place that protects their right to choose, their access to common resources or outside funds when it's needed, a way for them to get wherever they need to go, and their privacy. It should also leave room for the possibility that the community's preferred approach won't be enough.
P10: At the same time, being connected to people is measurably good for your health - the Surgeon General's advisory lists several health outcomes that isolated people are more at risk for. Community won't cure everything, but it can change the day-to-day conditions people get sick, heal, age, and die in.
